headline: On the Costa Blanca; vert banked, recon still owed
narrative: Vert came in a shade over target, though time on feet finished just under its ask. Be honest about the mix again: the two biggest climbing days were stair-machine sessions, ascent-only, no descent load. The genuine hill work was Wednesday's double loop over Higher Moor, and Sunday brought a rare double-run day — a hillier morning outing plus flat evening miles in proper heat. The quad took no flags all week, and the rehab lifting is still being done before the hard sessions, which is exactly the habit to keep.

The bigger story is location: Saturday's Altea run club means race terrain is now outside the front door. But the week's stated focus — a big back-to-back and the first course recon segment — didn't clearly happen; the weekend running was real but mostly flat. That work rolls forward with interest, because next week is the biggest vert ask of the entire build plus recon of the high mid-course. Being in Spain removes every excuse. Cumulatively the push toward the race stays on schedule; night running also remains owed.
